$comment: AUTO-GENERATED by packages/exponential-ui-bench/scripts/generate.ts — do not edit (inputs live in src/scenarios.ts). The Exponential UI benchmark suite (VAPP-105): one file per scenario under scenarios/, each naming its metrics. A runner (runners/, the core's and gpui's examples/bench_suite.rs, Swift's BenchSuiteTests, Compose's BenchSuiteTest) reports every scenario's non-optional metrics into a result fragment (src/results.ts); results/<machine>.json commits them per machine; budgets.json + scripts/ratchet.ts gate CI.

renderers.label: React · Chromium
renderers.pass: the DOM update flushed synchronously and the layout read back (main-thread work, no frame wait)

renderers.label: Solid · Chromium
renderers.pass: the signal writes applied synchronously (no scheduler) and the layout read back (as React: main-thread work, no frame wait)

renderers.label: Web component · Chromium
renderers.pass: one <exponential-surface> element: the property writes applied synchronously by the Solid painter underneath and the layout read back (as React and Solid)

renderers.label: Rust core
renderers.pass: one layout pass with a fixed fake measure (no text shaping, no painting)

renderers.label: gpui · headless
renderers.pass: the core pass plus gpui's own layout, prepaint and paint of a full frame (cosmic-text)

renderers.label: SwiftUI · macOS
renderers.pass: the model's pass: the core through the facade, TextKit measurement, nodes and visuals read back (no SwiftUI body)

renderers.label: SwiftUI · iPhone Simulator
renderers.pass: the model's pass on the Simulator (as macOS)

renderers.label: SwiftUI · iPhone
renderers.pass: the model's pass on an attached iPhone

renderers.label: Compose · JVM (Robolectric)
renderers.pass: the model's pass: the core through JNA, Robolectric's native text measure, nodes and visuals read back (no composition)

renderers.label: Compose · Android (emulator or device)
renderers.pass: the model's pass on the device (as the JVM, with the real text stack)

scenarios.title: Kitchen sink cold start
scenarios.what: The kitchen sink (every component of the core catalog once) painted by a renderer that has touched nothing yet: the embedded catalog and theme JSON parsed, the tree reduced, every macro expanded, data bound, text measured, laid out and painted. The cost an agent's first surface pays.

metrics.what: From the renderer's first touch in a fresh process (the first surface created: the catalog, macros and themes parse here) to the kitchen sink's first painted frame.

From the surface's content and data being handed to the renderer to its first painted frame: reduce + bind + measure + lay out + paint (a renderer without a window: the model's first pass). Generated data is built before the clock starts and handed over inside it (VAPP-149).
Placed nodes after the first paint (the reduced tree, template instances included).
The process's resident footprint after the scenario (RSS / phys_footprint; the JS heap in Chromium), in MB.
Heap allocations during the cold start (a counting allocator; the Rust core only).

scenarios.title: Card grid, warm width change
scenarios.what: The 205-node card grid (the core's bench tree): after the first paint, the surface alternates 390 and 900 px, so every pass re-resolves the grid's breakpoint, wraps the pills and re-measures nothing the width memo already answered. The engine's own time per pass.

metrics.what: Median of 200 passes alternating the width 900 ↔ 390 px (one pass = the width change applied, laid out and painted).
Measure upcalls (batched rounds) the core made per warm pass, max over the passes.
Text measurements the host performed per warm pass, max over the passes.

scenarios.title: 100,000-row list
scenarios.what: fixtures/bench-list.json, the shared list bench: a windowed List over 100,000 generated rows. First paint = bind + window + paint; a scroll step moves one viewport and re-windows; the jump lands on row 50,000. Where data binding and per-row text measurement cost.

metrics.what: From the surface's content and data being handed to the renderer to its first painted frame: reduce + bind + measure + lay out + paint (a renderer without a window: the model's first pass). Generated data is built before the clock starts and handed over inside it (VAPP-149).
Mean of 100 scroll steps of one viewport each (the scroll applied, the window re-bound, laid out and painted).
scrollToIndex(50000, start): the jump applied, the window re-bound, laid out and painted.
Items alive after the jump (≤ the window + 2 × overscan + the pinned header).
Text measurements the host performed per scroll step (mean).
Facade calls (host → core and the measure upcalls) per scroll step (mean; Swift and Compose, behind the debug counters).
Bytes of JSON and records crossing the facade per scroll step (mean; Swift and Compose, behind the debug counters).
The process's resident footprint after the scenario (RSS / phys_footprint; the JS heap in Chromium), in MB.

scenarios.title: Streaming agent
scenarios.what: An agent streaming 20 messages a second for 10 s: 200 messages alternating an updateComponents that appends one transcript card and an updateDataModel that moves a status line and a progress bar. Each message is applied, laid out and painted before the next. Where a renderer rebuilds too much per message.

metrics.what: Mean cost of one message: applied, laid out and painted.
The 95th percentile of that cost (the late messages, when the transcript is long).
All 200 messages back to back (must stay far under the 10 s they would arrive in).
Placed nodes after the first paint (the reduced tree, template instances included).
Bytes crossing the facade over the whole stream (Swift and Compose, behind the debug counters).

scenarios.title: Theme and mode switch
scenarios.what: The kitchen sink painted, then the theme cycled neutral → playful → exponential (every recipe re-resolves, every node restyles) and the mode flipped light ↔ dark (colours only). The cost of a runtime theme change on a full surface.

metrics.what: Median of 30 theme switches (the theme set, restyled, laid out and painted).
Median of 20 mode flips (the mode set, restyled, laid out and painted).
Nodes the core restyled on one theme switch (the whole tree is the honest answer).

scenarios.title: Resize 390 ↔ 900
scenarios.what: The kitchen sink resized between a phone and a desktop width, 100 times: the responsive section changes columns, the sidebar collapses and expands, the Drawer's side flips; text re-wraps at a new width. The cost of a window resize or a rotation.

metrics.what: Median of 100 width changes 900 ↔ 390 px (the width applied, measured, laid out and painted).
Measure upcalls (batched rounds) per resize, max over the passes.

scenarios.title: Depth-48 nesting
scenarios.what: A chain 48 levels deep, the catalog's maxDepth: every level a padded column with a label. 95 nodes, but every pass walks the full depth and the recursive passes (reduce, build, taffy) run at their limit.

metrics.what: From the surface's content and data being handed to the renderer to its first painted frame: reduce + bind + measure + lay out + paint (a renderer without a window: the model's first pass). Generated data is built before the clock starts and handed over inside it (VAPP-149).
Median of 100 passes alternating the width 900 ↔ 390 px.
The deepest placed node's level (the root = 1): must be 48.

scenarios.title: 10,000 template items
scenarios.what: A plain column (not a windowed List) with a template over 10,000 items, the catalog's maxTemplateItems: every item is instantiated and bound at once. Then the array is replaced by 10,000 new items. Pure template binding cost, no windowing to hide it.

metrics.what: From the surface's content and data being handed to the renderer to its first painted frame: reduce + bind + measure + lay out + paint (a renderer without a window: the model's first pass). Generated data is built before the clock starts and handed over inside it (VAPP-149).
The array replaced by 10,000 new items: re-bound, laid out and painted.
Placed nodes after the first paint (the reduced tree, template instances included).

scenarios.title: Overlay open and close
scenarios.what: A surface with a Dialog whose open state is bound to the data model: opened and closed 50 times through the binding. The layer manager, the focus trap and the overlay's own layout, per toggle.

metrics.what: Median of 50 opens (the binding set true, the layer placed, laid out and painted).
Median of 50 closes (the binding set false, the layer gone, laid out and painted).

scenarios.title: Table with 1,000 rows
scenarios.what: A data Table over 1,000 bound rows with typed columns (a badge, a right-aligned number): first paint, 20 scroll steps of one viewport, then the sort changed through an updateComponents. The Table's row binding and windowing against the List's.

metrics.what: From the surface's content and data being handed to the renderer to its first painted frame: reduce + bind + measure + lay out + paint (a renderer without a window: the model's first pass). Generated data is built before the clock starts and handed over inside it (VAPP-149).
Mean of 20 scroll steps of one viewport each.
The sort changed by an updateComponents: applied, rows re-ordered, re-bound, laid out and painted.
Rows alive after the scroll steps (a windowed Table keeps it near the viewport's).
